chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sayf ibn 'Umira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One who recites 'Ha-Mim-Ain-Sin-Qaf', Allah will raise him on the Day of Judgment with his face like snow or like the sun, until he stands before Allah, the Exalted and the Mighty.

It will be said to him: My servant, you were consistent in reciting 'Ha-Mim-Ain-Sin-Qaf' and did not know its reward. If you had known what it is and what its reward is, you would not have grown weary of reciting it.
But I will surely give you your reward. Make him enter Paradise.
And for him in it will be a palace of red ruby, its doors, turrets, and stairs; its exterior is visible from its interior and its interior from its exterior.
And a thousand pageboys from the eternal youths, whom Allah, the Exalted and the Mighty, described.

key_terms.حَمْعِسَق: Ha-Mim-Ain-Sin-Qaf (opening letters of a Surah, often referring to Surah As-Sajdah in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Ha-Mim-Ain-Sin-Qaf according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual merit of consistently reciting Surah Ha-Mim-Ain-Sin-Qaf (Surah As-Sajdah), promising a radiant countenance on the Day of Judgment as a sign of divine recognition. The reward is described with vivid imagery, including a palace of red ruby where the interior and exterior are mutually visible, symbolizing transparency and purity, accompanied by a thousand eternal pageboys. This reflects the Shia tradition of linking specific Quranic recitations with tangible eschatological rewards and divine intimacy.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Sayf b. ’Umayra from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

One who recites “Surah Sajdah”, Allah will raise him on the Day of Judgment while his face would be like the snow (delighted) or like the sun till he would be presented before Allah, the Exalted and the Mighty:

It will be said to him: My servant, you had regularly recited the “Surah Sajdah” and you did not know its reward. If you knew what it is and what is its reward you would not be shortcoming in reciting it;
and I will soon give your reward. O Angels make him enter Paradise
and in it will be a palace of red rubies, and its doors and turrets arches. He will see its inside from the outside and its outside from its inside
and a thousand pageboys born there and living there, whom Allah, the Exalted and the Mighty, had selected.”
